profile.name: Sushma Acharya
profile.title: Computer Engineer | NLP Researcher
profile.summary:
I am a computer engineer shaping my career in  Natural Language Processing (NLP) and computational social science, with experience spanning academic research, data analytics, backend development, and applied AI.

My research interests lie at the intersection of language, human behaviour, and digital wellbeing. I am particularly interested in understanding how people express emotions, communicate experiences, and reveal patterns of behaviour through their interactions in online spaces.

As an IEEE-published researcher, I enjoy combining computational methods with behavioural insights to explore meaningful questions about human experiences in the digital world. I aim to develop research that goes beyond analysing data to uncover the patterns, contexts, and human experiences behind it.

I am continuously exploring how NLP and AI can help us better understand people and the digital environments they inhabit.

heroParagraphs:
I began my academic journey with a Nepali-medium education and gradually found my way into computer engineering, research, and applied technology. Each transition challenged me to learn beyond what was familiar, strengthening my adaptability, independence, and curiosity.

Today, I bring together experience in academic research, data analytics, backend development, and applied AI as I shape my path toward natural language processing and computational social science. I am particularly interested in understanding how people express themselves, interact, and experience wellbeing in online spaces.

What motivates me is the opportunity to connect technical methods with meaningful human questions, using data not merely to identify patterns, but to better understand the experiences behind them.
Those experiences eventually led me toward computer engineering, academic research, and  backend development.

projects.title: Kidney Disease Prediction Systems project
projects.summary: A machine learning project focused on predicting chronic kidney disease from structured clinical data.
projects.description: This project explored how data preprocessing, feature analysis, and model comparison can support early disease prediction. It strengthened my foundation in data cleaning, evaluation, and interpreting technical results clearly.

projects.title: Drug Prescription Analysis
projects.summary: A data analytics project studying prescription patterns, trends, and decision support possibilities.
projects.description: This work focused on analyzing structured healthcare-related data to identify meaningful patterns, clean inconsistencies, and communicate findings through clear reporting and visual summaries.

projects.title: Social Media and Well-being Research
projects.summary: A research project examining how social media use relates to well-being, behavior, and digital habits.
projects.description: This project brought together research design, literature review, data interpretation, and academic writing. It became a key part of my transition story by sharpening how I investigate evidence and communicate structured findings.

projects.title: Prompt Search Analysis
projects.summary: An exploratory study of how people search, refine, and evaluate prompts in AI-assisted workflows.
projects.description: This ongoing research interest connects my curiosity about AI with my growing interest in quality. It looks at prompt behavior, clarity, reliability, and how structured evaluation can improve AI-supported work.

projects.title: QA Automation Sandbox
projects.summary: A learning-focused testing project for practicing API testing, regression thinking, and automation fundamentals.
projects.description: This sandbox supports my transition into QA by giving me a place to design test cases, document bugs, validate APIs, and gradually build automation habits around real testing scenarios.

projects.title: Portfolio Website
projects.summary: A personal portfolio built to present my transition from engineering and research into quality assurance.
projects.description: This site is both a portfolio and a narrative project. It connects my academic background, research work, backend experience, QA direction, and interest in AI-powered testing through a structured, modern interface. The public pages use HTML and CSS and can be hosted on GitHub Pages.

blogs.title: Why I’m Moving from Research and Backend Work into QA
blogs.excerpt: A personal note on how research, engineering, and curiosity about software quality brought me toward QA.
blogs.content: My transition into QA does not feel like starting over. It feels like bringing together everything I have already learned: how to ask better questions, how to analyze evidence, how systems behave internally, and how small issues affect user trust.

blogs.title: What Research Taught Me About Finding Better Bugs
blogs.excerpt: Research trained me to notice patterns, challenge assumptions, and document findings carefully. QA needs the same habits.
blogs.content: A good bug report is not just a complaint. It is evidence. Research helped me learn how to observe carefully, describe clearly, and support claims with detail, which translates directly into stronger testing work.

blogs.title: Testing APIs with a Backend Developer’s Perspective
blogs.excerpt: Understanding backend structure changes the way I think about API validation, edge cases, and reliability.
blogs.content: Because I have spent time working with backend logic, I often approach API testing by thinking through data flow, expected failure modes, and how small inconsistencies surface in real usage.

blogs.title: Building a Portfolio That Connects QA, AI, and Research
blogs.excerpt: A portfolio should not just list tools. It should explain the story that connects your skills and direction.
blogs.content: For me, the portfolio is a place to connect computer engineering, data analytics, research, backend development, and the shift into QA. The goal is not to appear scattered, but to show how each step built the next one.

blogs.title: Small QA Automation Projects as a Learning Strategy
blogs.excerpt: Automation becomes easier to learn when it grows from realistic testing habits instead of isolated syntax drills.
blogs.content: I am approaching automation through small, repeatable QA projects: testing APIs, checking core flows, and learning where scripts are genuinely useful. That keeps the learning practical and tied to software quality rather than only tooling.
